subsystems.name: Graphene additive
subsystems.role: provides nano-scale reinforcement and nucleation sites for cement hydration.

subsystems.name: Cementitious binder
subsystems.role: forms the matrix that binds aggregates; graphene allows less cement to be used.

subsystems.name: Aggregates
subsystems.role: provide bulk, dimensional stability and compressive strength.

subsystems.name: Admixtures
subsystems.role: control workability, setting time and air content.

subsystems.name: Mixing and placement
subsystems.role: combine all ingredients uniformly and place the concrete.

subsystems.name: Curing and quality control
subsystems.role: ensure proper strength development and verify performance.

buildSteps.title: Produce or source graphene
buildSteps.detail: Graphene oxide is made by oxidising graphite and exfoliating it; graphene nanoplatelets are made by liquid-phase exfoliation or other scalable methods.

buildSteps.title: Prepare a graphene dispersion
buildSteps.detail: The graphene powder is mixed with water and a dispersant, then treated with ultrasound or high shear to separate layers and prevent clumping.

buildSteps.title: Batch the concrete
buildSteps.detail: Cement, aggregates, water and admixtures are weighed and combined in a batching plant. The graphene dispersion is added at a controlled rate.

buildSteps.title: Mix thoroughly
buildSteps.detail: The wet mix is agitated in a concrete mixer, often for longer than conventional concrete, to distribute the graphene evenly.

buildSteps.title: Place and compact
buildSteps.detail: The concrete is poured into formwork and vibrated or compacted to remove trapped air.

buildSteps.title: Cure
buildSteps.detail: The concrete is kept moist and at a suitable temperature so that cement hydration proceeds and the graphene can template the growth of strong hydration products.

buildSteps.title: Test and verify
buildSteps.detail: Samples are tested for compressive and flexural strength, workability and durability to confirm the mix meets the design specification.

prerequisites.why: large volumes of consistent, low-cost graphene are needed for concrete, but current production is still relatively expensive.
graphene tends to agglomerate; achieving even dispersion in a truckload of concrete is difficult.
new materials must be tested and approved against building codes before structural use.
to verify that reduced cement content actually lowers embodied carbon.

pathway.milestone: pilot pours in non-structural or lightly loaded elements
pathway.unlocks: real-world performance data and contractor familiarity.

pathway.milestone: certification for structural use in specific applications
pathway.unlocks: use in columns, slabs and foundations where cement savings matter most.
mainstream adoption in infrastructure and buildings.

pathway.milestone: integration with other low-carbon cements and recycled aggregates
pathway.unlocks: deep cuts in the carbon footprint of concrete.
